text.p: NEUE ZUERCHER ZEITUNG - Swiss lower house of parliament ratified United Nation's Children Rights Convention. - Swiss insurer Winterthur reported a 24 percent rise in net profit to 248 million Swiss francs for the 1996 first half. - Migros Bank lowered its mortgage rate for first class mortgages by 0.25 percentage points to 4.5 percent. TAGES ANZEIGER - World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) started the biggest public campaign in its history. Named "The Living Planet", the projet is focusing on protecting endangered species and natural areas and preserving the sustainability of natural resources. - The Swiss advertising market in August shrunk by 2.7 percent compared with the same month last year. - Swiss high-tech group Esec reported a 71 percent rise in turnover to 138 million Swiss francs for the first semester of fiscal 1996/97. The group expects to double net profit and sales for the whole business year. JOURNAL DE GENEVE - Swiss left-wing member of parliament Jean Ziegler pleaded for a complete abolition of Swiss bank secrecy laws. - Swiss inflation rate remained at 0.6 percent. Swiss Index for Comsumer Prices registered a 0.1 percent rise compared to the month before.
